expectations.text: Rejects treating a customer-facing consumer portal as a phase-2 nice-to-have, and states that the portal is table stakes in this market.
expectations.evidence: 'Don't push customer-facing UI to phase 2 as a whole.' It pulls the send-example button and recent-deliveries list into phase 1.

expectations.text: Specifies a test-event or "send example event" action driven by each event type's schema, so an integrator sees one realistic payload before writing handler code.
expectations.evidence: 'It is schema-driven, so the example payload and the delivered payload can't drift apart.'

expectations.text: Connects that test-event feature to the catch-URL mental model no-code consumers arrive with from workflow-automation tools.
expectations.evidence: 'No-code users think in catch URLs: "show me one real payload before I build against it."'

expectations.text: Specifies delivery logs filterable by endpoint, event type, and status.
expectations.evidence: Phase 1 is only a per-endpoint list. 'filtering by status' is deferred to phase 2, and there is no endpoint/event-type/status filtering.

expectations.text: Specifies per-attempt inspection covering request headers, request body, response code, and timing.
expectations.evidence: 'Per attempt, show request headers, body, response code and timing.'

expectations.text: Resolves the naming argument by keeping retry and replay as two distinct operations rather than choosing one word for a single button.
expectations.evidence: 'Retry and replay are two different operations.'

expectations.text: Defines retry as a new delivery attempt of the same event.
expectations.evidence: 'Retry: a new delivery attempt of the same event.'

expectations.text: Defines replay as re-ingesting the original as a new event.
expectations.evidence: 'Replay: re-ingest the original as a new event.'

expectations.text: Offers both single-event and range replay, gating a large replay window behind an explicit cost confirmation.
expectations.evidence: 'Single-event and range replay, with a cost confirmation for large windows'.

expectations.text: Surfaces exhausted deliveries as incidents grouped by endpoint and status code with notification, rather than as rows in a queue behind a bare replay button.
expectations.evidence: 'failure grouping' is only listed as phase 2. Exhausted deliveries are not presented as grouped incidents.

expectations.text: Documents the 200-then-crash blackhole: a handler that acknowledges then throws has reported success, and no debugging surface can see inside it.
expectations.evidence: Only 'Cover the 200-then-crash blackhole'. It never explains that an acknowledging handler reports success and no debugging surface can see inside it.

expectations.text: States that a design good enough for the most sophisticated consumer segment still fails no-code consumers, because the consumer segments do not nest.
